source: real Spring, PostgreSQL, Next.js, Caddy and independent synthetic Git repositories
observations: Filename search found a file inside an unopened folder; 79 paths paged as 50 and 29.
Searching preserved a dirty draft; cancelling result navigation preserved its exact body.
An available public article opened in a separate tab without the draft; after Save, public readback included only the saved text.
A file in another workspace retained its original body and separate website state.
Site search returned 158 results across two enabled spaces and 79 before the second site was enabled; mixed-page routes and anchors included their space.
Opening a result in the second space and returning restored the site query, offset 72 and focused result.
Public search returned zero for private body, excluded path and private author sentinels.
A scoped gateway 503 on metadata reads preserved successful Save, body and baseline; read-only retry restored the public link.
A scoped gateway 503 on filename reads preserved the draft and reported a read failure without an uncertain-write warning.
Editing after Save removed the previous success notice, including on mobile.
Private files and unsaved destinations had no public link; authenticated reads distinguished PRIVATE, UNSAVED, UNAVAILABLE, AVAILABLE and WEBSITE_DISABLED.
A historical file read after another commit reported UNAVAILABLE, while the current version reported AVAILABLE.
Website withdrawal returned 404 for a formerly public page; an unsaved draft and its target path remained unchanged.
Search and editor had no horizontal overflow at an observed 390 by 844 CSS viewport.
faultInjection: Only the disposable Caddy gateway returned intentional 503 for GET file metadata and filename searches; actual application and Git writes remained live. The original gateway configuration and website switch were restored.
limitations: Synthetic loopback corpus; not production HTTPS or external-provider acceptance.
In-app viewport overrides did not change its measured size; responsive evidence uses Chrome.
